_readme: Every playable character. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id is written into save files, so never rename one after a save exists; role and attackType are matched case-insensitively against CharacterRole and DamageType, and CharacterEntryResolver rejects an unknown name at build time rather than shipping a character that silently falls through to the wrong Skill case. THE SIX ABILITY SCORES FOLLOW NO FIXED BUDGET: CharacterEntryResolver and ContentDatabase.ValidateContent check no total, so Shawn/Bjorn/Odette ship at 66/64/62. A character with no real weakness is a flatly stronger pick than the roster, so author a weak score for every strong one. Each score still has to be a plausible number on its own: refused below 1 or above 30 in the resolver, and outside 3-20 in the built-catalogue check. STAT SPREADS EXPRESS THE ROLE, so a squad's strengths are readable from its species alone, and attackType gives each character an elemental identity for the weakness/resistance system: three characters cover three of the six DamageType values, chosen by loose theme (wool/pasture, brute strength, old and wise) rather than min-maxed against the enemy roster. BOTH ART PATHS ARE RESOURCES-RELATIVE AND CARRY NO EXTENSION: portraitPath names one head-and-shoulders PNG under Resources/Portraits/ (the dossier plate) and battleSpritePath a folder of full-body stance art (the fight stage, produced by tools/slice_actor_sheet.py). Both load at runtime, so a row added here is complete the moment the content is rebuilt. The two conventions coexist elsewhere in content (iconPath, iconSheet are baked); ArtPathConvention is the one statement of which field is which. SIGNATURE RESOURCES are each character's own private combat resource; an EMPTY signatureId means the character has none — that is the meaningful distinction, not a zero capacity. WHICH POOL A CHARACTER'S SKILLS SPEND IS ALSO CONTENT: primaryPoolId names a row in pools.json and blank means mana, so trading mana for a different resource — a different capacity rule, different gains, different colours, and no spell books — is one field on this row rather than a special case in code (Bjorn's is `fury`). A signature resource rides the same three triggers (per-turn, on-attack, on-damage-taken), so a new one is content and wiring rather than a parallel system. Wool (Shawn) is the only one shipped today, and it is per-turn-led at base: the row authors signatureGainPerTurn 1 and nothing else (signatureGainOnAttack and signatureGainOnDamageTaken are 0), so a base Shawn banks exactly one wool a turn no matter what he does with it. Both income levers are content. The reward track pays SignatureGainPerTurn at 5 and SignatureGainOnDamageTaken at 19 (reward_tracks.json), and talents add other income: swearing to the Black Ram (sheep_ram_root) turns being hit into wool (WoolOnHitTaken) and pays more per turn the worse the day is going (WoolPerTurnBelowHealth at 67% and 33% health). Wool does NOT absorb damage: the row authors signatureAbsorbsDamage false, so ResourcePool.Absorb returns 0 and incoming damage goes straight to his health; no track reward switches it on, so wool is ammunition only. Whether the base row should ship absorbing is open (AUDIT #121). He starts every fight at zero, which is why he has the worst opening turn in the game and the best closing one. Bjorn spends fury instead, a pool rather than a signature (primaryPoolId, not signatureId, so none of the three signature triggers apply to it); Odette carries neither and spends plain mana. ALL THREE STARTING SPREADS ARE AUTHORED: Shawn (STR 12, DEX 10, CON 14, WIS 12, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 66), Bjorn (STR 12, DEX 12, CON 14, WIS 8, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 64) and Odette (STR 8, DEX 12, CON 8, WIS 12, INT 14, CHA 8 — total 62). baseStats (maxHealth, speed, attack, physicalDefense, magicalDefense) are separate from the ability scores: a character's EFFECTIVE stats (Health, Attack, Speed, Mana Regen, both DEF lines, Max Mana) move on their own, purely through AbilityDerivation, with nothing hand-tuned to compensate. ROSTER ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that silently reshuffles which characters land in the default squad (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). Three of the five CharacterRole values are covered by the shipped roster (Utility, Tank, Support); Assassin and CrowdControl are unclaimed, for whichever character ships next. plateArt is the character's OWN FIGHT-HUD PLATE -- the wide leather strip with their head embossed at the right end, which the fight column draws their name, meters and status badges on. Resources-relative and without an extension like the two art paths above, REQUIRED on every row, and refused at build time if the file loads nothing: the acting character is a highlight on their own plate now rather than a promotion to a bigger card, so a row without a plate has no face in the HUD at all. tools/normalize_pc_plates.py is what produces the file (it brings the owner's three separately-drawn strips to one canvas and one aspect) and docs/ART_PIPELINE.md section 1 registers the kit. plateTheme is the character's IDENTITY COLOUR, worn by the rim and the name of every fight-HUD card that stands for them (Domain.UiKit.PcTheme maps the theme to its two hexes); matched case-insensitively against UiKit.ButtonTheme and REQUIRED on every row -- an empty or unknown value refuses the build, because every valid value is some other character's colour. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.
